'''OS-72-8''' was the designation of a [[TIE pilot]] who served in the [[Imperial Navy/Legends|Imperial Navy]] by<ref name="CSWE" /> [[3 ABY/Legends|3 ABY]]. By that [[Standard year/Legends|year]],<ref name="NEC">''[[The New Essential Chronology]]''</ref> the [[Pilot/Legends|pilot]] was stationed aboard<ref name="CCG" /> the [[Imperial I-class Star Destroyer/Legends|Star Destroyer]]<ref name="CSWE OS">{{CSWECite|II|402|Obsidian Squadron}}</ref> [[Devastator/Legends|''Devastator'']], and had also joined the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Imperial]] [[Obsidian Squadron/Legends|Obsidian Squadron]], flying under the [[Callsign/Legends|call sign]] of [[Obsidian 8]]. While flying under the call sign of Obsidian 8, OS-72-8 flew a modified [[TIE/ln space superiority starfighter/Legends|TIE/LN starfighter]] used most often to pursue raiders attempting to take refuge in the upper [[Atmosphere/Legends|atmosphere]] of nearby [[Planet/Legends|planets]]. The pilot had also left the ''Devastator'' before<ref name="CCG" /> the Empire's [[Occupation of Bespin|occupation]] of the planet [[Bespin/Legends|Bespin]] in 3 [[Galactic Standard Calendar|ABY]].<ref name="NEC" />

During Bespin's occupation, the [[YT-1300 light freighter/Legends|YT-1300 light freighter]] [[Millennium Falcon/Legends|''Millennium Falcon'']] managed to escape the planet,<ref name="ESB">{{Film|V}}</ref> and OS-72-8 was among the [[TIE series/Legends|TIE]] pilots who subsequently pursued the [[Freighter/Legends|freighter]].<ref name="CSWE" /> However, the TIE [[Starfighter/Legends|fighters]] were unable to capture the ''Millennium Falcon'', with the freighter managing to evade Imperial capture in [[Realspace/Legends|space]].<ref name="ESB" />

==Behind the scenes==
The OS-72-8 name was first used for [[2003]]'s [[The Empire Strikes Back (TCG)|''The Empire Strikes Back'']] expansion set of [[Wizards of the Coast]]'s ''[[Star Wars Trading Card Game]]''. OS-72-8 was identified as the designation of a TIE fighter seen in<ref name="TCG">{{TCG|set=The Empire Strikes Back|cardname=TIE Fighter OS-72-8|link=https://swtcg.com/Content/Images/Cards/ESB/TIE_Fighter_OS_72_8.webp?v=2}}</ref> the [[1980]] [[original trilogy]] film [[Star Wars: Episode V The Empire Strikes Back|''Star Wars'': Episode V ''The Empire Strikes Back'']],<ref name="ESB" /> though [[Decipher]]'s [[1997]] ''[[Cloud City Limited]]'' expansion set of the [[Star Wars Customizable Card Game|''Star Wars'' Customizable Card Game]] had previously identified the fighter as "Obsidian 8."<ref name="CCG" /> The [[2008]] ''[[The Complete Star Wars Encyclopedia]]'' resolved the issue by identifying OS-72-8 as the pilot<ref name="CSWE" /> of the Obsidian 8 TIE fighter seen in ''The Empire Strikes Back''.<ref name="ESB" /> Before the film's [[May 21]], 1980 release,<ref name="Empire Turns 40">{{ThisWeek|6UccH037VQ0|The Empire Strikes Back Turns 40, Queen's Peril Gets a Voice, and More!|sw_url=video/the-empire-strikes-back-turns-40-queen-s-peril-gets-a-voice-and-more}}</ref> OS-72-8's fighter appeared simultaneously in ''[[The Empire Strikes Back Storybook]]''<ref name="ESB storybook">''[[The Empire Strikes Back Storybook]]''</ref> and the film's [[Star Wars: The Empire Strikes Back (novelization)|novelization]],<ref name="ESB novel">[[Star Wars: The Empire Strikes Back (novelization)|''Star Wars Episode V: The Empire Strikes Back'' novelization]]</ref> both released [[April 12]] of the same year.<ref name="Amazon-RandomHouse">{{Amazon|url=Empire-Strikes-Back-Storybook/dp/0394844149|text=The Empire Strikes Back Storybook}} {{C|US hardcover}}</ref><ref name="Year by Year">''[[Star Wars Year By Year: A Visual History, Updated and Expanded Edition]]''</ref>
